title: Call surface change scorer and rollback orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a runtime-side heuristic that scores changes to model invocation call surfaces and structured outputs, expose the score to rollout controller, and implement an orchestrator that can auto-hold or auto-rollback canary/A-B rollouts based on severity-weighted compatibility signals from shadow/canary traffic.
background: We frequently deploy model versions that change the structured output or function-call surface. Existing canary/shadow tooling flags diffs but gives little signal for prioritization or automated action. Ops spends time triaging thousands of small, non-actionable diffs. We need a compact score that encodes user-impact risk (breaking vs. additive) and enables conservative auto-rollback policies for high-severity regressions.
proposal: Build a Call Surface Change Scorer (CSCS) that ingests schema diffs and function-call signature deltas from the runtime probe and produces a numeric compatibility score plus categorical severity labels (OK, NOTICE, WARN, BREAK). Integrate CSCS into the rollout controller: during shadow/canary runs, compute aggregated scores per time window and trigger a hold/rollback policy when thresholds are exceeded. Also add a replay-based rollback-orchestrator that can replay failing invocations against the previous version to collect concrete mismatches before committing rollback decisions.
implementation_steps: Runtime probe: add a light-weight fingerprint + AST-lite comparer for structured outputs and function-call metadata (branch: feat/cscs-probe)
Scoring logic: implement heuristic that weights message fields by requiredness, type-change, enum-delta, and call-argument presence/absence
Telemetry: emit aggregated metrics (compatibility_score, pct_major_breaks, pct_minor_breaks) to metrics pipeline and to Console per-rollout dashboard
Policy: add new rollout controller policies: hold_if_score_gt, auto_rollback_if_major_pct_gt, and grace windows
Replay orchestrator: capture failing sample invocations and replay against previous model, store diff artifacts in GCS, attach to rollout event
Console UI: add compact compatibility-trend sparkline and top-5 changed function signatures in rollout details
E2E tests: synthetic workload that exercises function-calling and structured output permutations; shadow-run in staging at 2% for 72h
Runbook: document automatic rollback thresholds and manual escalation path for non-deterministic diffs
acceptance_criteria: CSCS produces a deterministic score for the same diff fingerprint across runs
Rollout controller can read CSCS signals and auto-hold when configured policy breaches at canary time-window
Replay orchestrator successfully replays at least 95% of captured failing invocations in staging and produces diff artifacts
Console displays compatibility metrics and links to replay artifacts in rollout UI
Shadow run for new model with synthetic schema changes shows alerting if major_breaks > 0.2% over a 1h window
Unit + integration tests added and PRs merged: runtime probe, controller policy, replay orchestrator, console panels
metrics: pct_major_breaks: fraction of invocations flagged MAJOR_BREAK
time_to_rollback: median time from policy-breach to rollback completion
false_positive_rate: manual rollbacks where replay shows no functional regressions
triage_load_reduction: reduction in ops tickets triaged for call-surface diffs (target 60% drop)
risks: Over-sensitive scoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks and customer disruption
Replay may be non-deterministic for stochastic models; risk of false positives
Telemetry volume growth if probes emit full payloads instead of fingerprints
Security/PII: replaying real requests into staging must be scrubbed; requires security review and KMS changes
notes: Replay artifact format: ndjson diffs + minimal context (request-token-hash, route, model-version)
Security: staged data-scrubber must run before replaying PII-bearing requests; added security review gate
